scope.working_tree: Current review fixes on this head

provenance: Current executable call paths independently inspected; the October 21 fm-main-backstop-review-inventory.json remains historical and is not the inventory for this change.

R2_review-1.invariant: Ownership and generation decisions observe one consistent PID/session record under the writer claim mutex.
R2_review-1.cause: Ownership readers bypassed the mutex while publication wrote the sidecar and PID separately.
R2_review-1.resolution: Use the existing acquisition mutex for a shared PID/session snapshot; actual mutex owners reuse their hold, ordinary readers wait through the existing acquisition lifetime. Observational holder reports use zero wait and report unknown when busy. Auto-arm claim inspection uses a zero wait to avoid lock-order inversion, and its busy status retains an otherwise live generation. The preliminary fm-lock admission probe also uses zero wait so the existing bounded-sweep fast refusal stays reachable; confirmation still owns the claim mutex. A busy preliminary snapshot skips live-holder classification and falls through to claim acquisition, preserving contended same-session confirmation and re-anchoring.
R2_review-1.regression: tests/fm-session-lock-ancestry.test.sh:test_takeover_boundaries_share_one_commit pauses with old PID and new session, probes both real process trees, checks live claim deferral, then checks only the successor owns after commit.

R3_review-2.invariant: A takeover aborts if holder turn evidence changes between its first scan and its final pre-publication scan.
R3_review-2.cause: The last scan preceded sidecar staging and did not retain evidence to detect even backdated added turns.
R3_review-2.resolution: Compare a digest of the holder turn UUID/timestamp list on every scan and re-scan after staging immediately before publication, under the claim mutex, for both startup and Stop. Stop carries its initial digest into the delegated acquisition as a restrictive comparison, including backdated additions before delegation.
R3_review-2.regression: Boundary tests append a current or backdated user turn during sidecar staging and require unchanged ownership, no handover, no arm and intact leases for startup and Stop. The Stop delegation boundary also appends a backdated turn before fm-lock starts.
R3_review-2.remaining_bound: UserPromptSubmit is intentionally uncoupled. The normally sub-second interval after the final scan remains; scheduler stalls can extend it. This is revalidation, not an atomic physical-input admission guarantee.

R4_R10.invariant: Every uncommitted takeover preserves predecessor ownership and task exclusion, regardless of whether lease migration began.
R4_R10.cause: Rollback was gated on leases moving, and a newly allocated backup was not necessarily complete.
R4_R10.resolution: Only phase 2 can have changed the PID; it starts after backup completion and restores the predecessor pair on abort. Phase 1 restores only the sidecar. Reverse rekeying alone depends on the lease-movement flag.
occurrences: bin/fm-lock.sh:on_lock_exit, publication, verification, lease rekey, handover append
R4_R10.regression: Boundary tests cancel backup creation, session publication, PID verification, lease movement and journal preparation for startup and Stop; prior partial lease-move failure regression and both actor guards are retained.

R5_review-3_R9.invariant: Every live holder of a watcher-silent home reaches one named inbox ask after fifteen minutes, without repeated silence nudges.
R5_review-3_R9.cause: Foreground PID equality bypassed the holder ask, and documentation conflated queueing with owner notification.
R5_review-3_R9.resolution: Remove foreground discovery/exemption from the holder branch, preserve existing durable inbox delivery and request deduplication, and describe the working main as the owner-notification actor.
occurrences: bin/fm-main-backstop.py:main live-holder silence branch and deliver_alarm
tests/fm-main-backstop.test.py:queued holder ask and foreground-holder tests
R5_review-3_R9.regression: Backstop tests drive silence below and above fifteen minutes for foreign and foreground holders, assert one durable note and wake with PID/TTY/idle, and assert zero pane submissions.

R6_R7_retained.invariant: Disabled capability cannot discover or submit to a primary; discovery returns only the pane consumed by all callers.
R6_R7_retained.resolution: Remove the unused PID tuple under R15, retaining capability-before-discovery and isolated real-Herdr session guards.

R8.invariant: The next review and validation receive a current class inventory with executable regressions and explicit evidence limits.
R8.resolution: Current inventory retained here and linked from both verification records, with actual focused results, current real-Claude proof and explicit platform, transport, timing and fixture-cleanup gaps.

R11.invariant: A quiet holder rekeyed from A to B permits a fork of A or B, but never one with unreadable, recent or changed holder histories.
R11.cause: The sidecar discarded A on clear, so the shared predicate could prove only B.
R11.resolution: Retain the immediately prior SID as row 2 of the existing sidecar for ancestry-owned rekeys; validate and scan both histories at the shared predicate and compare both in the pre-publication digest. Confirmation preserves lineage; takeover publishes only its new SID.
occurrences: fm-claude-stop-autoarm.sh:initial proof and delegated digest comparison
R11.regression: Both startup and Stop test A/B acceptance and unrelated, recent, missing, changed and malformed-prior refusal; live guard invokes native clear, refuses an unrelated real fork and accepts resume A.

R12.invariant: Claim contention cannot discard valid ownership or generation admission during an existing bounded sweep.
R12.cause: The new five-second cap was shorter than the ordinary 120-second sweep lifetime.
R12.resolution: Default ownership snapshots use existing fm_lock_acquire_wait; preliminary admission, claim inspection and diagnostic reports explicitly request nonblocking reads.
R12.regression: A six-second claim hold must still allow an owning Stop to arm and a subsequent generation claim to admit.

R13_R14.invariant: One classified report determines holder identity, note key and retirement; proven stale holders permit recovery, while unknown observations preserve incidents.
R13_R14.cause: A kill(0)-only PID observation preceded a separate report and conflated non-harness or unreadable identity.
R13_R14.resolution: Use one state=held/free/stale/unknown shell report; classify verified non-harness and absent PIDs stale, keep read failures unknown, and derive the episode key only from the reported held PID.
occurrences: fm-main-backstop.py:holder_report, silence branch, nudge eligibility, episode retirement
R13_R14.regression: Real reused non-harness PID permits nudge; live and dead-PID ps failures retain episode; a handover injected before the report creates exactly one successor-keyed ask.

Inspected existing serialization: cmd_run takes .lock.acquire, rechecks expected PID under it, retains it across fm_run_timed bootstrap, and releases only after the child completes. FM_BOOTSTRAP_NETWORK_LOCK_PID is set only at that guarded call. Their PID-only comparisons already run under the writer mutex; acquiring again in the child would wait on its parent, so those production paths remain unchanged.
